static_traits.name: Ma Yisen
static_traits.medical_history: Denying similar problems in the past; no prior psychological counseling/treatment history; no major physical illness mentioned
static_traits.language_features: Expression is clear, able to concretely describe events and feelings; the tendency to self-criticism is obvious, often using absolutist self-labels; willing to cooperate with plans such as 'behavioral experiments'; hesitant about seeking help from others, inclined to bear it alone

basic_info.main_problem: After losing a rope during naval work, causing a boat to drift away and need recovery, continuously labeling themselves as 'I am an idiot/incompetent', ruminating frequently, especially intensifying self-doubt when facing new tasks, affecting work performance and self-esteem.
basic_info.core_demands: Because feelings of incompetence and self-doubt are affecting my work performance and self-esteem, I am seeking counseling.
growth_experiences: An operational mistake once occurred in the naval post: losing a rope, causing a boat to drift away and need recovery. The pressure was great at the time, and the client partly attributed the cause to the pressure of 'having to perform perfectly'. In the following months they repeatedly recalled the event, forming the self-label 'I am an idiot/incompetent'; self-doubt and worry rose markedly especially when facing new tasks, with attention and execution decreased in efficiency.

core_beliefs: I am incompetent/I am an idiot
Only perfect performance counts as valuable

special_situations.event: Facing new tasks or work challenges not yet attempted
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot complete this perfectly, it proves my incompetence, and I will make mistakes like last time
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Bearing pressure alone, reducing help-seeking, trying to persuade oneself with reason but worrying repeatedly
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I am going to mess up again this time

special_situations.event: Recalls the accident of losing the rope, causing the boat to drift away
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: One major mistake equals me being a failure overall
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly ruminates on mistakes, uses negative labels to drive oneself to prevent recurrence

special_situations.event: After completing some tasks smoothly (such as leading a drill that finished early), reviewing performance
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Only major or perfect achievements 'count', average success does not represent ability
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Ignores or discounts positive evidence and keeps magnifying the impact of mistakes
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: These successes are useless, not enough to prove I am not an idiot

special_situations.event: Thinking of confiding troubles to colleagues or family and friends and seeking support
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: I should not trouble others, exposing vulnerability will be looked down on
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoiding expression and asking for help; choosing to bear it alone

core_conflict.wish: Being seen as capable, reliable, and gaining recognition and trust
core_conflict.fear: Fearing mistakes will be judged as incompetence, suffering shame and negation, and thus losing opportunities and belonging
defense_goal: Controls risk and avoids exposing vulnerability and seeking help through self-criticism and high standards, to maintain a sense of 'safety' and controllability

object_relations.self_representation: Prone to mistakes, needing constant self-vigilance, a 'potentially out-of-control/incompetent person'
object_relations.object_representation: 'Strict judges/superiors and others' who may judge and negate them at any time

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When counseling focuses on the emotional experience and impact of mistakes
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing emotions should be controlled, using rational narratives to avoid appearing vulnerable or incompetent
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: States facts in an objective, calm tone, emphasizes 'it was just one mistake / too much pressure', minimizing emotional expression.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When invited to consider seeking support from colleagues or family
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Others will be impatient with my distress or look down on me (transferentially attributing negative evaluation to others)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Politely but firmly deflecting suggestions to seek help, emphasizing 'not wanting to trouble others', downplaying real available support.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When talking about responsibility attribution or evaluating one's ability
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Internalizes complex external factors as own defects, tending to blame all faults on self
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Using self-blame and negative labels (e.g. 'I am an idiot'), ignoring situational factors and positive evidence.

manifestations: Unwilling to confide distress to colleagues or family and friends, worrying about 'troubling others' or being looked down on, choosing to bear pressure and unease alone
outcomes: Lacking social support, rumination and self-doubt worsen
Emotional burden hard to share, attention and decreased work efficiency

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or things, or gives up seeking others to do something for them, and instead does it to the self, turning the energy originally meant to be sent outward toward the self.
manifestations: Not expressing needs outwardly when support is needed, choosing to 'carry it alone'
When troubled, replacing seeking help and communication with self-blame and self-reproach

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths.
manifestations: Takes 'must be perfect' as an internal criterion; judges himself by success or failure in an all-or-nothing way

contact_model.definition: The individual has maladaptive self-reflection, containing excessive self-limitation and self-reproach, being overly cautious about contact.
manifestations: Frequent self-criticism and labeling ('I am an idiot')
Avoiding expressing vulnerability in front of others, overly cautious to prevent being judged

exception_events.target_problem: When facing new tasks or work challenges not yet attempted, usually strongly doubting themselves due to the last mistake and worrying about erring again, leading to distracted attention and decreased work efficiency.
exception_events.unique_outcome: Serving as a squad leader in a team drill, the process went smoothly and finished ahead of schedule, with good team cooperation; at the time he felt 'I know what I am doing', and confidence briefly rose.
exception_events.reason: Clues: clear task goals and processes, good team execution, clear role authority; he focused on steps and communication rather than outcome success or failure, lowering anxiety and maintaining effective focus.

positive_force: Has the experience and ability to successfully lead teams and manage tasks
Willing to try and cooperate with corrective strategies such as 'behavioral experiments'
Able to identify and describe their own negative thought patterns
Strong sense of responsibility, willing to improve performance
negative_force: Perfectionism and strict value conditions (not perfect means incompetent)
Ignoring positive evidence, focusing only on mistakes (mental filtering/negating the positive)
Anticipatory worry about future failure, prone to catastrophizing when facing new tasks
Avoiding seeking help, insufficient use of social support

target_behavior.behavior: Strong self-blame and rumination with automatic thoughts of 'I am an idiot/will mess up' around new tasks, accompanied by decreased attention and reduced efficiency
target_behavior.core_reason: Overgeneralizing one mistake as overall incompetence, and binding self-worth to perfect performance; maintaining control and security through self-blame
target_behavior.function: Through self-criticism to 'prevent repeating the mistake / stay highly vigilant', and avoiding the emotional risk of facing potential failure
target_behavior.consequence: Persistent rumination and anxiety impair focus and execution, decline in work performance, damaged self-esteem

target_behavior.behavior: Avoiding seeking support and confiding in colleagues or relatives and friends, choosing to bear it alone
antecedent: When encountering difficulties or emotional distress and needing help
When thinking one may need to communicate with others for help
target_behavior.core_reason: Introjecting the rule of 'not troubling others', worrying about being judged or looked down on, tending to suppress needs inward
target_behavior.function: Avoiding the possibility of being rejected or shamed, maintaining surface self-control and dignity
target_behavior.consequence: Insufficient social support, negative thoughts and emotions hard to buffer, problems maintained or worsened
